title: The Verdict Doesn't Wait
tagline: Closing arguments due by five, a client who won't stop second-guessing you, and a witness who just went off script.

wake_up.text: Trial day. Closing arguments are due by end of day, and the draft on your desk still isn't the one you want to give.

choices.text: Rewrite the closing argument one more time before you leave
Trust last night's draft and get moving

morning_prep.text: Case files spread across the back seat, coffee going cold, the courthouse twenty minutes out.

choices.text: Head to the courthouse

random_moment.text: The walk from the parking garage to the courthouse steps has its own small rhythm every morning — a little different each time.

choices.text: A reporter outside the courthouse asks for a quick comment
An old colleague from law school catches you for a quick hello
You catch an easy parking spot for once

client_meeting.text: Your client is in the consultation room, visibly shaking. "What if the jury doesn't believe me?" is not a question there's a clean answer to this morning.

choices.text: Take the extra time to reassure them properly before court
Keep it brief — court starts in twenty minutes

jury_arrival.text: The jury files in. Twelve strangers who are about to decide something that will follow your client for the rest of their life.

choices.text: Court is called to order

trial_begins.text: The prosecution calls its key witness sooner than expected. Your cross-examination notes are ready — mostly.

choices.text: Prepare for cross-examination

witness_cross.text: Mid cross-examination, the witness says something that isn't in any statement you've seen before — a detail that could help your client, or could be a trap. The jury is watching you decide what to do with it, right now.

choices.text: Press hard on the new detail immediately
Probe gently to see where it leads before committing
Object and request a brief recess to consult your notes
Pivot away from it and stick to your planned line of questions

cross_outcome_aggressive.text: The pressure pays off — the witness contradicts their earlier statement under the weight of your questions, right in front of the jury. It's the kind of moment that decides trials.

choices.text: Finish the cross-examination

cross_outcome_gentle.text: The careful approach draws the witness out further than a direct challenge would have, and they say more than they meant to. Patience, this time, was the sharper tool.

choices.text: Finish the cross-examination

cross_outcome_recess.text: The judge grants a short recess. Your notes confirm the detail is real and usable — but the jury watched you need to stop and check, and juries notice hesitation.

choices.text: Resume the cross-examination

cross_outcome_pivot.text: You stay on script. It's safe, and it leaves an opening on the table that the prosecution's redirect examination picks up on almost immediately.

choices.text: Finish the cross-examination

lunch_recess.text: A short recess before the afternoon session. Your client wants to talk through what just happened; your closing argument still needs work.

choices.text: Spend the recess with your client instead
Use every minute to polish the closing argument

closing_prep.text: Afternoon session resumes. The prosecution rests. It's almost time.

choices.text: Prepare to deliver the closing argument

closing_argument.text: You stand, and the courtroom goes quiet in the particular way it does right before a closing argument. Everything from this case funnels down to the next fifteen minutes.

choices.text: Lead with the human stakes of the case
Walk the jury methodically back through the evidence

jury_deliberation.text: The jury files out to deliberate. There is nothing left to do now but wait, which is its own particular kind of exhausting.

choices.text: Stay at the courthouse in case they come back fast
Step out for air and clear your head

verdict.text: Word comes down: the jury has reached a verdict. You head back into the courtroom, and for a moment none of the last twelve hours matter as much as the next thirty seconds.

choices.text: Hear the verdict

end_shift.text: Whatever the jury decided, the courthouse empties out the same way it does every night — slowly, and then all at once.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: Case of the Year
triumphant.blurb: Every call today held up, including the one that mattered most. This is the case other attorneys will ask you about for years.

steady_hand.title: Solid Representation
steady_hand.blurb: No fireworks, no theatrics — just careful, competent lawyering from open to close.

ordinary_day.title: Another Trial
ordinary_day.blurb: A full trial day, argued and closed. Tomorrow there's another file on the desk exactly like it.

burned_out.title: Running on Fumes
burned_out.blurb: You made it through closing arguments, but you're not sure how. This pace, case after case, has a real cost.

written_up.title: Bar Complaint Pending
written_up.blurb: Something about today's tactics is going to draw scrutiny. The trial is over. The questions about how it was tried aren't.
